namesake.match: Match each unit to the person it is named after.

rows.label: joule
rows.description: SI unit of energy, work and amount of heat
rows.hook: measures energy and work, and is the amount a one-watt device uses each second

rows.label: degree Fahrenheit
rows.hook: is the temperature scale used in the United States, where water freezes at 32 and boils at 212

rows.label: degree Celsius
rows.hook: is the metric temperature scale where water freezes at zero and boils at one hundred

rows.label: kelvin
rows.hook: is the scientific temperature unit whose zero point is absolute zero, the coldest possible

rows.label: decibel
rows.description: logarithmic unit expressing the ratio of a physical quantity
rows.hook: measures how loud a sound is, and is named for the inventor of the telephone

rows.label: pascal
rows.description: SI unit of pressure and stress
rows.hook: measures pressure, and is named for a French thinker who also built an early calculating machine

rows.label: hertz
rows.hook: measures how many times something repeats each second, such as a sound wave or radio signal

rows.label: watt
rows.hook: measures power, and is printed on light bulbs to show how much electricity they draw

rows.label: newton
rows.hook: measures force, and is named for the scientist said to have been inspired by a falling apple

rows.label: ampere
rows.hook: measures the flow of electric current, and is the unit fuses and circuit breakers are rated in

rows.label: ohm
rows.description: SI derived unit of electrical resistance
rows.hook: measures how strongly a material resists the flow of electricity, and is written with the Greek letter omega

rows.label: coulomb
rows.hook: measures electric charge, equal to what a one-amp current carries past a point in a second

rows.label: volt
rows.description: SI unit of electric potential, of electric potential difference (voltage), and of electromotive force
rows.hook: measures electrical pressure, such as the 1.5 on a AA battery or 120 from a US wall outlet
